name: Markup
tagline: Pin comments directly on websites, images, PDFs and videos so reviewers stop sending vague emails.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core mechanic is a pin with a comment thread anchored to coordinates on an asset, and that is genuinely a weekend build. Images and PDFs are easy: upload, render, click to drop a pin, store x/y plus a thread, share a read-write link. Live website review is where it gets ugly, because proxying someone else's site into an iframe fights CSP, breaks on auth walls, and re-anchoring pins across viewport widths is a real engineering problem rather than a Saturday one. You can dodge that by screenshotting the URL with Playwright and annotating the capture, which covers most actual design feedback but loses the interactive click-through review. Video annotation with timestamped pins is doable but adds another day.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted review board where you upload an image or PDF or paste a URL for a Playwright screenshot, then anyone with the share link drops numbered pins with comment threads and resolves them.
requirements: Node 20 and a place to run it that reviewers can reach (VPS or a tunnel)
Playwright with Chromium installed for URL screenshots
Local disk or S3-compatible storage for uploads and captures
Reviewers willing to use a link with a shared secret instead of real accounts
whatYouLose: True live-site review: clicking through real pages, hover states, logged-in flows, mobile/tablet/desktop breakpoints with pins that survive reflow
Video review with timestamped comments and frame-accurate scrubbing
Integrations that push comments into Jira, Asana, Trello, Slack, so feedback never leaves the tool
Email notification plumbing, digests, @mentions and the nagging that actually makes reviewers respond
Client-facing polish: someone non-technical opening the link on a phone and it just working, plus a browser extension
moatNotes: The moat is not the pin, it is that a client with no account can open a link on any device and it never glitches. That reliability is what you are actually paying for.
whyPeopleStillPay: Markup sits between you and a paying client, which means every rough edge in your DIY version becomes an awkward email. A self-hosted board is fine for your own team and terrible for the moment a stakeholder says the link is broken on their iPad. Add the Jira and Slack pushes, the notification emails that keep a review from stalling for a week, and the fact that live interactive review is a genuinely hard rendering problem, and the seat fee stops looking like laziness.
notes: The pin-and-thread part is a weekend; the part where a client's browser cooperates is the whole product.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted visual feedback tool called Pinboard in this empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Playwright with Chromium for URL captures. No auth provider, no cloud services, no telemetry, no analytics.

Data model in SQLite:
- projects: id, name, created_at
- assets: id, project_id, kind ('image' | 'pdf' | 'url_capture'), source_url (nullable), file_path, width, height, page_count, created_at
- pins: id, asset_id, page (default 1), x_pct, y_pct, number, status ('open' | 'resolved'), created_at
- comments: id, pin_id, author_name, body, created_at
Store x and y as percentages of rendered asset width/height so pins stay put when the viewer is resized.

Features that are in scope:
1. Create a project. Upload PNG/JPG/PDF, or paste a URL and capture a full-page screenshot with Playwright at 1440px wide, saved to ./storage/captures.
2. Asset viewer: render the image, or render PDFs page by page (server-side rasterize to PNG at load time is fine, keep it simple). Click anywhere to drop a numbered pin and open a comment composer.
3. Pins render as numbered dots. Clicking one opens a side panel with the thread, a reply box, and a Resolve toggle. Resolved pins render hollow and can be hidden via a filter.
4. Author name is stored in localStorage and prompted once, no accounts.
5. Share links: /a/[assetId]?t=TOKEN where the token is a per-project random string stored in the projects table. No token, no access. Anyone with the token can read and comment.
6. Project dashboard listing assets with open pin counts.
7. Export a project's pins and comments as JSON and as a plain markdown checklist.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt: live iframe proxying of third-party sites, responsive breakpoint switching, video annotation, email notifications, real user accounts, roles, Jira/Slack integrations, mobile app.

Config: .env with STORAGE_DIR and SQLITE_PATH, plus a generated APP_SECRET. Ship .env.example, never commit .env.

Deliver a README with setup, npx playwright install chromium, dev and prod commands, and a one-paragraph honest note that URL captures are static screenshots and not interactive site review. Seed script that creates one demo project with a sample image and two pins.
